column2: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, drooping face, slurred speech, or sudden loss of vision or balance
Weakness or numbness

Agree on a stop signal (the word “stop” or a raised hand) before you begin; the person giving the massage asks every 1–2 minutes “how is the pressure?” (target: 4–6 out of 10), and the recipient can ask at any time for lighter, firmer or stopping, without explanations. On request, or with sharp pain, numbness or dizziness, stop immediately. In pregnancy, skip GB21 (step 2) and ask the doctor for approval. Pressure goes into the muscle, not deep, without tilting the head back. If dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, weakness in one arm or new, intense pain in the back of the neck appears, stop and call 112.

Make fists and place the knuckles on GB30, in the hollow of the buttock, at the junction of the outer and middle thirds of the line between the tip of the greater trochanter and the sacral hiatus. Let your weight build up gradually to 3–5 out of 10, not deep; keep one hand on the chair or the wall. Breathe slowly; you can also use two tennis balls between the wall and the buttocks.
Call 112 now. Do not drive yourself to the hospital and do not continue the massage or acupressure.
Traditionally used for forearm fatigue; possible muscle relaxation, with no evidence for “tennis elbow” pain and not a substitute for a medical consultation.

In pregnancy, ask the doctor for advice before PC6. If you have carpal tunnel syndrome, reduce the pressure. Chest pain, strong palpitations or fainting: stop and call 112.

In pregnancy, ask the doctor for advice. Nausea with chest pain or pressure, sweating, shortness of breath, severe headache, intense dizziness, weakness or slurred speech: call 112. Repeated vomiting, fever, strong abdominal pain, signs of dehydration (dry mouth, little urine) or vomiting during pregnancy: medical consultation the same day. During chemotherapy, talk to the oncology team.

In pregnancy, do not massage the soles, ankles and hand (LI4, SP6, BL60, LR3, SP4, KI3) unless the doctor or midwife approves. With diabetes and reduced sensation in the foot, only with the doctor's approval.
In pregnancy, skip CV3–CV7 and any pressure on the abdomen. No pressure with abdominal or inguinal hernia, heavy menstruation, abdominal inflammation or acute pain.

In pregnancy, skip CV12 and ST25 completely (abdominal area). No pressure with abdominal or inguinal hernia, active ulcer, abdominal inflammation, recent procedures, cirrhosis or fluid in the abdomen, known abdominal aortic aneurysm, stoma or pump, heavy menstruation or acute abdominal pain (especially lower right, with fever or vomiting: possible appendicitis, do not press and see a doctor). Do not begin if you have repeated vomiting, a swollen and hard abdomen, you are not passing gas or stool, you see blood in the stool or vomit, you have flank pain with fever, or your period is late and pregnancy has not been ruled out.
In pregnancy: caution. Avoid this point or ask the doctor or midwife for approval.

Before anything else, look at and feel both calves: if one is more swollen, warmer, red or painful to pressure, especially after a long trip, immobilization, surgery, during pregnancy or after childbirth, do not massage and go to the emergency department the same day (with shortness of breath or chest pain: 112). Also: severe varicose veins, edema, wounds, inflamed skin.
